title: Anthropic seeks rehearing of case over Pentagon's security risk branding
source_used: Reuters (text read on its copy at The Economic Times, marked 'By Reuters')
key_facts: Anthropic asked a US appeals court in Washington, DC, on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) to reconsider a ruling that upheld the Pentagon's decision to label it a national security supply chain risk over a dispute about safety guardrails (Reuters).
A federal appeals court upheld the designation 2-1 in September, agreeing with the Pentagon that Anthropic's safety restrictions could compromise military operations.

The majority said the Pentagon acted reasonably after Anthropic refused to allow its AI to be used in autonomous weapons or mass surveillance, and rejected Anthropic's claim that it faced retaliation over its views on AI safety.
Anthropic's petition says the panel majority misinterpreted and transformed a federal law 'aimed at hostile foreign actors into one that presumptively reaches every government contractor'.
Anthropic says the court let the Pentagon act 'without any pre-designation process and despite straightforward evidence the designation was retaliation for Anthropic's speech about AI safety'.
Anthropic has said the Pentagon's blacklisting has cost it billions of dollars in lost business.
In a separate lawsuit in August, a federal judge in California struck down a parallel designation under a different law.
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has called for regulation covering all US frontier AI companies, while the Trump administration has favored a pro-growth approach.
quote_evidence: Anthropic asked a US appeals court on Tuesday to reconsider a ruling that upheld the Pentagon's decision to label the AI company as a national security supply chain risk over a dispute about safety guardrails on its technology.
A federal appeals court in September upheld the designation in a 2-1 decision, agreeing with the Pentagon that the firm's safety restrictions could compromise military operations.
why_it_matters_hint: A rehearing request keeps open the question of whether the Pentagon can blacklist a US AI firm over its safety limits.
event_date: Petition filed Tuesday 13 Oct 2026; the ruling it challenges was made in September 2026 (2-1).
